text:
To: All Regional Managers
From: Daniela Ortiz, Logistics Director
Subject: Revised delivery schedule

Following last week's port strike, shipments of seasonal inventory will reach our distribution center roughly ten days later than [1]. [2] Stores that depend on these items for the holiday promotion should therefore review their floor plans immediately. Our freight partner has assured us that the backlog at the terminal is being cleared strictly in order of arrival and should be gone by the end of the month. The delay is regrettable. [3], it does not affect regular orders, which remain on the original timetable. We are also negotiating with a second carrier, which should help us to [4] the impact of any comparable disruption in the future. Please direct any questions about individual orders to the logistics help desk before Friday.

questions.explanation: 'Later than planned' requires the past participle, as in 'than expected'. 'Planning', 'plan' and 'to plan' cannot follow 'than' in this comparison.

choices: Several managers have already asked whether the strike could be extended into the following month.
Carriers have been told that late arrivals will no longer be accepted at the docks after six p.m.
Regular stock will continue to be shipped from the secondary warehouse in the northern region.
The affected merchandise includes winter apparel, gift sets and festive lighting for the displays.
questions.explanation: 'These items' in the next sentence needs an antecedent naming the delayed seasonal goods, which only the sentence about winter apparel, gift sets and festive lighting provides. Regular stock, the possible extension of the strike and the dock rules do not describe items for the holiday promotion.

The sentence contrasts the regrettable delay with the good news that regular orders are unaffected, which 'nevertheless' expresses. 'Consequently' implies a result, 'similarly' implies a parallel and 'specifically' introduces a detail.

A second carrier would help to 'mitigate' the impact of a future disruption, meaning reduce it. 'Aggravate', 'exacerbate' and 'perpetuate' all suggest making or keeping a problem worse, which contradicts the purpose of the negotiation.

text:
NOTICE TO RESIDENTS
Hawthorne Court Apartments

The building's heating system will undergo a scheduled upgrade between October 14 and October 18. During this period, hot water will be [1] between 6 a.m. and noon each day. [2] Residents who rely on early-morning showers are advised to adjust their routines accordingly.

Engineers will need access to each unit to inspect the radiators, so tenants are asked to ensure that the areas around them are [3]. If you will not be at home, please leave a key with the front desk by October 12. Residents with medical needs that require a continuous supply of hot water should speak to the building manager as soon as possible so that alternative arrangements can be made.

Management apologizes for any inconvenience and is confident that the improvements will [4] energy costs by roughly fifteen percent over the winter.

questions.explanation: Hot water cut off during set hours is 'unavailable' to residents. 'Unacceptable' expresses a judgment, 'unfamiliar' describes something not known, and 'unaffordable' refers to cost, none of which describes a supply interruption.

choices: Normal service will resume at noon each day, although hot water will then remain unavailable until the next morning.
Normal service will resume at noon on the final day only, and hot water will then remain available until the next morning.
Normal service will resume at 3 p.m. each day, and hot water will then remain available until the next morning.
Normal service will resume at noon each day, and hot water will then remain available until the following morning.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence sets the daily cut as 6 a.m. to noon, so service returning at noon every day is consistent, and it explains why only early-morning showers are affected. Resuming at 3 p.m. contradicts the stated window, resuming 'on the final day only' conflicts with 'each day', and 'unavailable until the next morning' contradicts 'normal service'.

After 'ensure that the areas ... are', the adjective 'clear' means free of obstacles so engineers can reach the radiators. 'Clearing' is a gerund, 'clearly' is an adverb, and 'clearance' is a noun, so none of them completes the passive-style structure.

Improvements in heating efficiency are expected to 'reduce' energy costs by about fifteen percent. 'Reproduce' means to copy, 'restore' means to bring back, and 'respond' is intransitive, so none of them takes 'energy costs' as an object in this sense.

text:
IMPORTANT NOTICE FOR PASSENGERS
Coastal Ferry Lines

Due to forecast high winds on Wednesday, the 7:15 a.m. and 9:45 a.m. departures from Port Ellis have been canceled. [1] This service will operate as scheduled unless conditions worsen, in which case an announcement will be made at the terminal. Passengers holding tickets for the canceled services may [2] their travel to a later date without charge or request a full refund. [3] passengers who booked online, a refund will be issued automatically to the card used for payment. Refunds requested at the terminal will be processed within seven working days. Passengers who have already checked in their luggage should collect it from the baggage hall before leaving the terminal. We recommend that you [4] our website or call the information line before setting out, as services may change at short notice. We regret any inconvenience this may cause.

choices: Passengers who traveled yesterday were advised to join the 12:30 p.m. sailing, for which additional capacity had been arranged.
Passengers who must travel today are advised to cancel their journey, for which a full refund has been arranged.
Passengers who must travel today are advised to join the 9:45 a.m. sailing, for which additional capacity has been arranged.
Passengers who must travel today are advised to join the 12:30 p.m. sailing, for which additional capacity has been arranged.
questions.explanation: 'This service will operate as scheduled' needs a preceding sentence that names a service still running, which is the 12:30 p.m. sailing. The 9:45 a.m. sailing has been canceled, the past-tense sentence refers to yesterday, and advising passengers to cancel leaves 'this service' without a referent.
Ticket holders may 'transfer' their travel to a later date, meaning move it. 'Convert', 'redeem' and 'reserve' do not combine with 'to a later date' in this sense.
'As for passengers who booked online' introduces a specific group to whom the automatic refund applies. 'Instead of', 'owing to' and 'regardless of' make no sense before a group of passengers.
After 'we recommend that you' the base form is used: 'that you consult our website'. 'Consulted', 'consults' and 'consulting' do not fit this subjunctive structure.

text:
Dear Valued Customer,

At Greenfield Insurance, we are committed to providing coverage that evolves with your needs. After reviewing your policy, we have identified several changes that will take effect on January 1. [1] Your annual premium will increase by 3 percent, which is lower than the average rise across the industry. [2], your coverage limit for personal belongings will rise from $20,000 to $25,000, at no extra cost. We have also simplified the claims process: you can now submit a claim directly through our mobile app, and you will receive a decision [3] five business days of submitting it. If you have questions about any of these changes, our advisers are available to [4] you through them by telephone or in person at any of our branches. Your current policy number, GF-20417, remains unchanged. Thank you for your continued loyalty.

Margaret Doyle
Customer Relations Manager

choices: The principal changes affect your premium and your coverage limit, and we describe both of them in detail below.
Most of these changes concern your claims process, and we describe the new procedure in detail on the reverse.
None of these changes affects your premium or your coverage limit, and we describe the claims process below.
These changes were introduced last year, and details of the premium and coverage limit are available on request.
questions.explanation: The following sentences deal with the premium and then the coverage limit, and the claims process is introduced later with 'also', so the preceding sentence must announce the premium and the limit. A statement that none of the changes affects them, changes 'introduced last year' (against 'will take effect on January 1'), and a focus on the claims process each clash with what follows.

The 3 percent premium rise is a drawback and the higher coverage limit is a benefit, so 'However' marks the contrast. 'Consequently' and 'accordingly' would present the increase in cover as a result of the rise in premium, and 'instead' implies a substitution that the text does not describe.
'Within five business days of submitting it' is the standard time-limit expression. 'During', 'by' and 'for' cannot be followed by 'five business days of submitting' in this sense.
Advisers 'guide' customers through the changes, meaning they explain them step by step. 'Guard', 'guarantee' and 'gauge' do not take 'you through them'.

text:
Subject: Changes to the Dunmore Museum membership program

Dear Members,

After extensive consultation with visitors, the board has decided to restructure the museum's membership program from the start of next year. [1] Under this arrangement, annual membership fees will remain unchanged for individuals, but family memberships will rise by $10 to cover the cost of the new children's workshops. The galleries will also stay open until 8 p.m. every Thursday.

[2], all members will receive priority booking for special exhibitions, a benefit previously reserved for the highest tier. In return, the free guest passes that members once enjoyed will be discontinued, since they were [3] used. We understand that some of you may be disappointed by this change, and we would welcome your comments before the new rules take effect. Feedback can be [4] by e-mail to membership@dunmore.example until December 15.

Warm regards,
The Membership Team

choices: The board has therefore adopted a simpler structure with just three tiers, although the current five will be kept.
The board has therefore rejected a simpler structure with just three membership tiers in place of the current five.
The board has therefore adopted a simpler structure with three tiers in place of the five, effective last January.
The board has therefore adopted a simpler structure with just three membership tiers in place of the current five.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'Under this arrangement', which needs a structure that has been adopted; 'has therefore adopted a simpler structure with three membership tiers' supplies it and matches 'has decided to restructure'. 'Rejected' leaves no arrangement, keeping the current five tiers contradicts the restructuring, and 'effective last January' conflicts with 'from the start of next year'.

'Moreover' adds a further benefit to the extended Thursday opening hours already announced. 'Otherwise' introduces an alternative, 'nevertheless' expresses contrast, and 'for instance' would present priority booking as an example of the opening hours, which it is not.
The passes were discontinued because they were 'rarely used', which justifies removing them. 'Routinely', 'widely' and 'fully' describe heavy use, which would not be a reason to withdraw the benefit.
The passive 'Feedback can be submitted' requires the past participle. 'Submitting' and 'submit' cannot follow 'can be' in a passive, and 'submission' is a noun.

text:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

The annual school trip to the National Science Museum will take place on Friday, October 3. Students in grades eight and nine will leave by coach at 8 a.m. and return at approximately 4 p.m. [1] Each student should bring a packed lunch, a water bottle, and a notebook for the activities planned by the museum's education team. The cost of the trip, $18 per student, [2] the entrance fee and transport. Payment should be made by Friday, September 19, using the school's online system. A permission form is enclosed and must be returned by Friday, September 12. [3] you prefer that your child not take part, please inform the school office in writing, and an alternative program will be arranged. Students are expected to behave [4] and to follow the instructions of the accompanying teachers at all times.

Yours faithfully,
Mrs. Janet Okoro
Head of Science

choices: Students will spend the morning at the museum, with a guided tour at nine and a laboratory workshop at five.
Students will spend the day at school, with a guided tour in the morning and a laboratory workshop in the afternoon.
Students will spend the day at the museum, with a guided tour in the morning and a workshop in the afternoon.
Students in grade seven will spend the day at the museum, with a guided tour and a laboratory workshop.
questions.explanation: The trip is to the museum, leaves at 8 a.m., returns around 4 p.m. and involves only grades eight and nine. Spending the day at school, scheduling a workshop at five o'clock after the return, or including grade seven all contradict the details given in the letter.
The fee 'covers' the entrance fee and transport, meaning it pays for them; 'exempts', 'deducts' and 'refunds' do not describe what a fixed price pays for.
'Should you prefer that your child not take part' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if'; 'unless' would reverse the logic of the request, and 'whether' and 'whereas' do not introduce a condition.
The verb 'behave' is modified by an adverb, so 'behave responsibly'; the adjective forms and the noun cannot modify a verb.

text:
To: Warehouse Supervisors
From: Marcus Obi, Safety Officer
Subject: New forklift procedures

Following two minor accidents in the loading area last month, new forklift procedures will come into force on Monday. [1] Only employees who hold a current certificate may operate a forklift, and certificates will be checked at the start of every shift. [2] Pedestrians must keep out of the marked lanes, and anyone who needs to cross them must wait until the driver has signaled that it is safe to do so. A speed limit of five miles per hour will be [3] throughout the building, and drivers found exceeding it will have their certificate suspended pending a review. Supervisors are asked to [4] these rules at their next team meeting and to report any breach to my office immediately. A refresher course for drivers is planned for the end of the month.

choices: The procedures are intended to keep vehicles and pedestrians apart and to make every driver individually accountable.
The procedures are intended to speed up loading times and to make every driver individually accountable for deliveries.
The procedures were intended to keep vehicles and pedestrians apart, and every driver was made accountable.
The procedures will apply only to the loading area, where both of the recent accidents took place.
questions.explanation: The sentences that follow list safety rules on certificates, marked lanes and speed, so the preceding sentence gives their purpose: keeping vehicles and pedestrians apart. Speeding up loading is not a safety aim, 'only the loading area' contradicts the speed limit 'throughout the building', and the past tense clashes with procedures that 'will come into force on Monday'.
'In addition' adds a second set of rules, for pedestrians, to the certificate rule. 'Otherwise', 'nevertheless' and 'instead' would imply an alternative or a contrast that the text does not contain.
'Will be enforced' is the passive future needed with 'a speed limit' as the subject. 'Enforce', 'enforces' and 'enforcing' cannot follow 'will be' to form a correct passive.
Supervisors are asked to 'emphasize' (stress) the rules at their team meeting. 'Empower' means to give authority, 'employ' means to hire or use, and 'emulate' means to imitate.

text:
Senior Data Analyst – Castellan Logistics

Castellan Logistics, a global freight forwarder, seeks a Senior Data Analyst to lead a team of four in our Rotterdam office. [1] In this capacity, the successful candidate will transform complex operational data into clear recommendations for senior management.

[2] To meet this requirement, applicants must hold a master's degree in statistics or a related field, together with five years of experience in a similar role. Fluency in English and Dutch is [3], as is the ability to explain technical findings to non-specialists. We provide a competitive salary of €72,000 to €80,000, relocation assistance, and the chance to [4] a team that is shaping the future of the industry. Interested applicants should submit their CV and a cover letter by December 1. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview in the week of 12 December.

choices: The department reports directly to the Chief Operating Officer and has grown rapidly since the merger with Veltra Freight.
The position reports directly to the Chief Operating Officer and plays a central role in strategic planning.
This position is open to internal and external applicants and will be filled before the end of the year.
The previous analyst reported directly to the Chief Operating Officer before leaving to join a competitor in March.
questions.explanation: 'In this capacity' needs a preceding sentence that describes the role itself, and the one stating that the position reports to the Chief Operating Officer does so. Describing the department, the previous analyst or the recruitment process gives the phrase no role to refer to.

choices: The role clearly demands rigorous statistical training and extensive experience with very large sets of operational data.
The company provides rigorous statistical training and extensive support for staff working with very large sets of data.
Candidates should expect a rigorous selection process, including extensive tests on very large sets of operational data.
The previous analyst had rigorous statistical training and extensive experience with very large sets of operational data.
questions.explanation: 'To meet this requirement' needs a preceding sentence stating what the role requires, which the sentence about the role demanding statistical training and experience does. Training offered by the company, the profile of the previous analyst and the selection process are not requirements that a degree and five years could satisfy.
An adjective is needed after 'is', and 'as is the ability' shows that a requirement is being compared: 'is essential'. The adverb and the nouns cannot function as a subject complement here.
One 'joins a team', meaning becomes a member of it. 'Enter' does not collocate with 'team', 'merge' needs 'with' and 'belong' needs 'to'.

text:
To: Project Leaders
From: Dr. Sunita Rao, Research Director
Subject: Budget submissions for next year

The budget cycle for the coming fiscal year will open on September 1. [1] These must set out expected costs, staffing requirements, and anticipated outcomes. Because funding is limited, proposals will be evaluated according to their alignment with the strategic priorities approved by the board. [2] Projects that rely on external partners must therefore include signed letters of support, [3] these cannot be considered. Please use the revised template available on the intranet; questions should be sent to Ms. Okafor in my office. Submissions should be uploaded to the shared drive by October 14, and late entries will not be reviewed. I would urge you to consult your finance officer before finalizing the figures, as several rules have [4] since last year.

choices: Project leaders are asked to confirm the external partnerships for the research programmes they intend to run next year.
Project leaders are asked to submit funding proposals for the research programmes that they intend to run next year.
Project leaders are asked to review the funding rules for the research programmes they ran during the past year.
Project leaders are asked to attend the briefing on the research priorities they will be expected to follow this year.
questions.explanation: 'These must set out expected costs, staffing requirements, and anticipated outcomes' needs a plural noun that can set out such details, and only 'funding proposals' qualifies. 'Rules', 'priorities' and 'partnerships' cannot set out costs and staffing.

choices: Priority will be given to work that makes use of the existing laboratory facilities and the equipment already in stock.
Priority will be given to work carried out independently by the department rather than with outside organisations.
Priority will be given to work carried out jointly with universities and industry rather than to stand-alone projects.
Work carried out jointly with universities and industry was favoured last year but will receive no preference now.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says projects relying on external partners 'must therefore' provide letters of support, so the preceding sentence must give priority to partnership work. Favouring independent work, existing facilities or 'no preference now' gives no reason for the 'therefore'.

'Failing which these cannot be considered' means 'if they do not include the letters, the projects cannot be considered'. 'In which case', 'following which' and 'regarding which' yield contradictory or meaningless statements.

'Several rules have been revised since last year' is the present perfect passive, since the rules are acted upon. 'Have revised' would make the rules the agent, and 'have revising' and 'have being revised' are not valid forms.

text:
A Quiet Revolution in Warehouse Design

The modern warehouse bears little resemblance to the dusty storerooms of the past. At the new distribution center in Hartlepool, which employs about nine hundred people, robots carry shelves to human pickers, [1] walking distances that once accounted for most of a worker's day. [2] Managers say this has raised productivity by nearly 60 percent since the system, which cost the company roughly 14 million pounds, was installed. Not everyone is convinced, [3]. Union representatives point out that the pace of work is now dictated by machines, and that injuries from repetitive movements have in fact increased from 31 to 47 cases a year. The company says it is [4] its procedures in response. Observers expect other firms in the logistics sector to follow suit if the gains prove to be sustainable over the coming two years.

questions.explanation: 'Thereby eliminating' is a participle phrase giving the result of the robots' work. 'Thus eliminate' and 'hence eliminated' do not fit after the comma, and 'whereas' introduces a contrast that the sentence does not make.

choices: Orders that once took under one minute to assemble now typically require several minutes, owing to extra safety checks.
At the company's older site in Leeds, orders still take several minutes to assemble, as no robots have been installed there.
Orders that once took several minutes to assemble are now typically completed in well under one minute at each station.
Rival firms have since copied the layout, and several of them have abandoned it after finding it too costly to maintain.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says that 'this' has raised productivity, so the preceding sentence must describe an improvement that explains it, such as faster order assembly. Slower orders would contradict the productivity gain, the older site in Leeds is not the system installed in Hartlepool, and the rivals' experience cannot be what raised productivity there.

The sentence contrasts the managers' claim with doubters, and 'however' can stand at the end of a sentence after a comma. 'Therefore', 'moreover' and 'likewise' do not express contrast and are not used in that position.
After 'it is' the present continuous requires the -ing form: 'is reviewing its procedures'. The other forms would not form a correct verb phrase after 'is'.
